content:
pranav: quick RFC follow-up — proposing autotune heuristics for kernel selection. TL;DR: bucket seq-len into [<=64,65-256,257-1024,>1024], prefer FP16/quant kernels when GPU occupancy < 60%, warmup 3 steps per new batch-shape, cache kernel choices per model+seq_bucket+device, fallback after 200ms of kernel selection latency. PTAL
marie: short — love the buckets. question: why 3 warmup steps? seems low for LRU cache thrash
pranav: 3 is empirical from local perf runs (numbers in the RFC). tradeoff: longer warmup increases tail for first requests. we can make it adaptive: warmup until measured kernel latency stabilizes within 5% over last N calls
alex: adaptive warmup sounds right. also we need to track 'batch shape' not just batch size: (batch, seq) tuple matters for kernel heuristics
sophia: for caching, can we use sticky cache per-customer so noisy multi-tenant workloads don't evict others? add tenant_id into the cache key
pranav: agreed — cache key = model#ver + device_type + seq_bucket + batch_shape_hash + tenant_policy. default tenant_policy=shared, but dedicated customers can request pinned cache
devon: kernel selection latency concern: can selection run asynchronously? start with a safe kernel for low tail-latency, probe better kernels in background and switch when stable
marie: +1 async probe. we should emit telemetry for probes: tags = model, device, seq_bucket, batch_shape, latency, memory_used
pranav: probe budget proposal: 5% of traffic per seq_bucket, capped at 1000 probes/day per cluster. probes should be rate-limited by tenant to avoid noisy neighbours
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout scheduled to eng-runtime-canary at 02:00 UTC (canary=5% traffic) :rocket:
alex: batch-shaping heuristics: bundling window should be adaptive. if queue wait > 3ms, shorten window to prioritize latency; otherwise allow up to 8ms to improve throughput. also split batches if avg_seq_len exceeds current seq_bucket upper bound
sophia: KV-cache policy: if prefix cache hit rate > 0.6 we keep pinned KV entries until model upgrade or idle timeout (default 10m). also expose tenant override
pranav: decision summary: 1) seq buckets = <=64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024; 2) use (batch,seq) batch_shape in keys; 3) adaptive warmup with 5% stability threshold; 4) probe 5% traffic, cap 1000/day; 5) async selection with safe-kernel fallback after 200ms; 6) tenant-aware cache keys with pinning for dedicated customers
marie: any objections? if none I'll mark this RFC-followup accepted and schedule work in Q2 sprint
devon: infra ok, will update perf harness and latency dashboards
sophia: no objections. can we add a follow-up to validate thresholds (3ms, 8ms, 5% stability) with a larger benchmark?
alex: LGTM :thumbsup:
pranav: thanks all — I'll open the RFC update with pseudocode and perf tables, assign owners for kernel selector, cache, and telemetry. sample cache key: `cache_key = f"{model}:{ver}:{device}:{seq_bucket}:{batch_hash}:{tenant}"`
